sanskrit: na tv eva manye puruṣasya karma; saṃvartate suprayuktaṃ yathāvat mātuḥ pituḥ karmaṇābhiprasūtaḥ; saṃvardhate vidhivad bhojanena
english: I do not think a man's action yields its full fruit in proper measure; born through the deeds of mother and father, he grows according to rule, sustained by food.

sanskrit: priyāpriye sukhaduḥkhe ca rājan; nindāpraśaṃse ca bhajeta enam paras tv enaṃ garhayate 'parādhe; praśaṃsate sādhuvṛttaṃ tam eva
english: O king, a man receives what is pleasant and unpleasant, happiness and sorrow, blame and praise; another blames him for a fault and praises that very same man when he behaves virtuously.

sanskrit: sa tvā garhe bhāratānāṃ virodhād; anto nūnaṃ bhavitāyaṃ prajānām no ced idaṃ tava karmāparādhāt; kurūn dahet kṛṣṇavartmeva kakṣam
english: I blame you for this strife among the Bhāratas; the end of the people will surely come, unless checked — for your transgression in deed will burn the Kurus as a wildfire burns dry grass.

sanskrit: tvam evaiko jātaputreṣu rājan; vaśaṃ gantā sarvaloke narendra kāmātmanāṃ ślāghase dyūtakāle; nānyac chamāt paśya vipākam asya
english: O king, you alone among those who have sons will come under subjection in all the world, O lord of men; you boasted at the time of the dice among those given to desire — see now the fruit of that, and know there is no remedy but peace.

sanskrit: anāptānāṃ pragrahāt tvaṃ narendra; tathāptānāṃ nigrahāc caiva rājan bhūmiṃ sphītāṃ durbalatvād anantāṃ; na śaktas tvaṃ rakṣituṃ kauraveya
english: O lord of men, by favouring those who are unworthy and by suppressing those who are worthy, O king, you are unable, through weakness, to protect this vast and boundless flourishing earth, O Kaurava.

sanskrit: anujñāto rathavegāvadhūtaḥ; śrānto nipadye śayanaṃ nṛsiṃha prātaḥ śrotāraḥ kuravaḥ sabhāyām; ajātaśatror vacanaṃ sametāḥ
english: Having been granted leave, shaken by the speed of the chariot and wearied, O lion among men, I now lie down to rest; tomorrow the Kurus will assemble in the hall as listeners to the words of Ajātaśatru.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dvāḥsthaṃ prāha mahāprājño dhṛtarāṣṭro mahīpatiḥ viduraṃ draṣṭum icchāmi tam ihānaya māciram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The greatly wise Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the earth, said to the doorkeeper, 'I wish to see Vidura — bring him here without delay.'

sanskrit: prahito dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa dūtaḥ kṣattāram abravīt īśvaras tvāṃ mahārājo mahāprājña didṛkṣati
english: The messenger sent by Dhṛtarāṣṭra said to Kṣattā: 'O greatly wise one, the great king, your lord, wishes to see you.'

sanskrit: evam uktas tu viduraḥ prāpya rājaniveśanam abravīd dhṛtarāṣṭrāya dvāḥstha māṃ prativedaya
english: Thus addressed, Vidura reached the king's palace and said to the doorkeeper, 'Announce me to Dhṛtarāṣṭra.'

sanskrit: dvāḥstha uvāca viduro 'yam anuprāpto rājendra tava śāsanāt draṣṭum icchati te pādau kiṃ karotu praśādhi mām
english: The doorkeeper said: 'O lord of kings, this Vidura has come in accordance with your command; he wishes to see your feet — command me, what shall he do?'

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca praveśaya mahāprājñaṃ viduraṃ dīrghadarśinam ahaṃ hi vidurasyāsya nākālyo jātu darśane
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: 'Bring in the greatly wise Vidura of far-sighted vision; for I am never at an inopportune moment for seeing this Vidura.'

sanskrit: dvāḥstha uvāca praviśāntaḥpuraṃ kṣattar mahārājasya dhīmataḥ na hi te darśane 'kālyo jātu rājā bravīti mām
english: The doorkeeper said: 'Enter the inner chambers of the wise great king, O Kṣattā; for the king tells me that he is never at an inopportune moment for seeing you.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ praviśya viduro dhṛtarāṣṭraniveśanam abravīt prāñjalir vākyaṃ cintayānaṃ narādhipam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Vidura entered the dwelling of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and, with hands joined in reverence, addressed the lord of men who was deep in thought.

sanskrit: viduro 'haṃ mahāprājña saṃprāptas tava śāsanāt yadi kiṃ cana kartavyam ayam asmi praśādhi mām
english: Vidura said: 'O greatly wise one, I Vidura have come at your command; if there is anything to be done, here I am — command me.'

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca saṃjayo vidura prāpto garhayitvā ca māṃ gataḥ ajātaśatroḥ śvo vākyaṃ sabhāmadhye sa vakṣyati
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: 'Vidura, Sañjaya has arrived and, having reproached me, he has gone; tomorrow he will speak the words of Ajātaśatru in the midst of the assembly.'

sanskrit: tasyādya kuruvīrasya na vijñātaṃ vaco mayā tan me dahati gātrāṇi tad akārṣīt prajāgaram
english: I have not yet learned what that hero of the Kurus will say, and this burns my limbs; it has caused me sleeplessness.

sanskrit: jāgrato dahyamānasya śreyo yad iha paśyasi tad brūhi tvaṃ hi nas tāta dharmārthakuśalo hy asi
english: Tell me what you see as the highest good for me, who am awake and burning with anxiety; for you, dear Vidura, are skilled in matters of righteousness and worldly gain.

sanskrit: yataḥ prāptaḥ saṃjayaḥ pāṇḍavebhyo; na me yathāvan manasaḥ praśāntiḥ sarvendriyāṇy aprakṛtiṃ gatāni; kiṃ vakṣyatīty eva hi me 'dya cintā
english: Since Sañjaya has returned from the Pāṇḍavas, my mind is not fully at rest; all my senses have gone out of their natural state — my anxiety today is only this: what will he say?

sanskrit: vidura uvāca abhiyuktaṃ balavatā durbalaṃ hīnasādhanam hṛtasvaṃ kāminaṃ coram āviśanti prajāgarāḥ
english: Vidura said: 'Sleeplessness visits the weak man who is attacked by the strong, one who lacks means, one whose wealth has been taken, one tormented by desire, and a thief.'

sanskrit: kaccid etair mahādoṣair na spṛṣṭo 'si narādhipa kaccin na paravitteṣu gṛdhyan viparitapyase
english: O lord of men, I hope you are not touched by these great faults; I hope you are not burning with longing for the wealth of others.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca śrotum icchāmi te dharmyaṃ paraṃ naiḥśreyasaṃ vacaḥ asmin rājarṣivaṃśe hi tvam ekaḥ prājñasaṃmataḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: 'I wish to hear your righteous words of supreme well-being, for in this lineage of royal sages you alone are acknowledged as truly wise.'

sanskrit: vidura uvāca niṣevate praśastāni ninditāni na sevate anāstikaḥ śraddadhāna etat paṇḍitalakṣaṇam
english: Vidura said: 'One who is devoted to what is commendable and does not pursue what is censured, who is not a skeptic but full of faith — this is the mark of a wise man.'

sanskrit: krodho harṣaś ca darpaś ca hrīstambho mānyamānitā yam arthān nāpakarṣanti sa vai paṇḍita ucyate
english: He whom anger, elation, arrogance, false modesty, vanity, and self-conceit do not drag away from his purposes — he is truly called a wise man.

sanskrit: yasya kṛtyaṃ na jānanti mantraṃ vā mantritaṃ pare kṛtam evāsya jānanti sa vai paṇḍita ucyate
english: He whose intentions and deliberated counsel others do not know, but only learn of what he has already accomplished — he is truly called a wise man.

sanskrit: yasya kṛtyaṃ na vighnanti śītam uṣṇaṃ bhayaṃ ratiḥ samṛddhir asamṛddhir vā sa vai paṇḍita ucyate
english: He whose purposes are not obstructed by cold, heat, fear, pleasure, prosperity, or adversity — he is truly called a wise man.

sanskrit: yasya saṃsāriṇī prajñā dharmārthāv anuvartate kāmād arthaṃ vṛṇīte yaḥ sa vai paṇḍita ucyate
english: He whose active intelligence follows righteousness and worldly gain, and who chooses wealth through proper desire — he is truly called a wise man.

sanskrit: yathāśakti cikīrṣanti yathāśakti ca kurvate na kiṃ cid avamanyante paṇḍitā bharatarṣabha
english: The wise undertake tasks according to their ability and execute them according to their ability; they despise nothing, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ vijānāti ciraṃ śṛṇoti; vijñāya cārthaṃ bhajate na kāmāt nāsaṃpṛṣṭo vyupayuṅkte parārthe; tat prajñānaṃ prathamaṃ paṇḍitasya
english: He comprehends quickly, listens patiently, and having understood the matter pursues it free from selfish desire; he does not interfere in another's affairs unbidden — this is the foremost wisdom of a wise man.

sanskrit: nāprāpyam abhivāñchanti naṣṭaṃ necchanti śocitum āpatsu ca na muhyanti narāḥ paṇḍitabuddhayaḥ
english: Men of wise intellect do not desire what is unattainable, do not grieve over what is lost, and are not bewildered in times of calamity.

sanskrit: niścitya yaḥ prakramate nāntar vasati karmaṇaḥ avandhyakālo vaśyātmā sa vai paṇḍita ucyate
english: He who sets out only after deliberating fully, who does not halt midway in an undertaking, who wastes no time and is master of himself — he is truly called a wise man.

sanskrit: āryakarmaṇi rajyante bhūtikarmāṇi kurvate hitaṃ ca nābhyasūyanti paṇḍitā bharatarṣabha
english: The wise delight in noble actions, perform deeds that bring prosperity, and do not envy what is beneficial to others, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: na hṛṣyaty ātmasaṃmāne nāvamānena tapyate gāṅgo hrada ivākṣobhyo yaḥ sa paṇḍita ucyate
english: He who does not exult at personal honour and is not distressed by dishonour, remaining unshakeable like a deep pool of the Gaṅgā — he is called a wise man.

sanskrit: tattvajñaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ yogajñaḥ sarvakarmaṇām upāyajño manuṣyāṇāṃ naraḥ paṇḍita ucyate
english: A man who knows the true nature of all beings, who understands the right application of all actions, and who knows the proper means among men — he is called a wise man.

sanskrit: pravṛttavāk citrakatha ūhavān pratibhānavān āśu granthasya vaktā ca sa vai paṇḍita ucyate
english: He who is eloquent in speech, a vivid narrator, gifted with inference, possessed of ready insight, and able to expound a text swiftly — he is truly called a wise man.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ prajñānugaṃ yasya prajñā caiva śrutānugā asaṃbhinnāryamaryādaḥ paṇḍitākhyāṃ labheta saḥ
english: He whose learning is in accord with wisdom and whose wisdom is in accord with learning, and who does not transgress the boundaries of noble conduct — he attains the designation of wise man.

sanskrit: aśrutaś ca samunnaddho daridraś ca mahāmanāḥ arthāṃś cākarmaṇā prepsur mūḍha ity ucyate budhaiḥ
english: One who is unlearned yet arrogant, one who is poor yet haughty, and one who seeks wealth without effort — the learned call him a fool.

sanskrit: svam arthaṃ yaḥ parityajya parārtham anutiṣṭhati mithyā carati mitrārthe yaś ca mūḍhaḥ sa ucyate
english: He who abandons his own interest to pursue another's, and he who acts deceitfully in the name of friendship — such a one is called a fool.

sanskrit: akāmān kāmayati yaḥ kāmayānān paridviṣan balavantaṃ ca yo dveṣṭi tam āhur mūḍhacetasam
english: He who desires those who do not desire him, who hates those who do desire him, and who harbours enmity toward the powerful — they call him a man of foolish mind.

sanskrit: amitraṃ kurute mitraṃ mitraṃ dveṣṭi hinasti ca karma cārabhate duṣṭaṃ tam āhur mūḍhacetasam
english: He who makes a friend of an enemy, who hates and injures a friend, and who undertakes wicked actions — they call him a man of foolish mind.

sanskrit: saṃsārayati kṛtyāni sarvatra vicikitsate ciraṃ karoti kṣiprārthe sa mūḍho bharatarṣabha
english: He who entangles his tasks in endless complications, who hesitates about everything, and who takes a long time over what should be done quickly — he is a fool, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: anāhūtaḥ praviśati apṛṣṭo bahu bhāṣate viśvasaty apramatteṣu mūḍhacetā narādhamaḥ
english: He who enters without being invited, speaks at length without being asked, and places trust in the vigilant — such a fool is the lowest of men.

sanskrit: paraṃ kṣipati doṣeṇa vartamānaḥ svayaṃ tathā yaś ca krudhyaty anīśaḥ san sa ca mūḍhatamo naraḥ
english: He who blames another for a fault while committing the same himself, and he who grows angry though he has no power — he is the most foolish of men.

sanskrit: ātmano balam ajñāya dharmārthaparivarjitam alabhyam icchan naiṣkarmyān mūḍhabuddhir ihocyate
english: He who does not know his own strength, who, devoid of righteousness and wealth, desires what cannot be obtained while doing nothing — he is called one of foolish intellect in this world.

sanskrit: aśiṣyaṃ śāsti yo rājan yaś ca śūnyam upāsate kadaryaṃ bhajate yaś ca tam āhur mūḍhacetasam
english: O king, he who instructs one who is not a worthy pupil, who attends upon a worthless person, and who serves a miser — they call him a man of foolish mind.

sanskrit: arthaṃ mahāntam āsādya vidyām aiśvaryam eva vā vicaraty asamunnaddho yaḥ sa paṇḍita ucyate
english: He who, having attained great wealth, learning, or lordship, moves about without arrogance — he is called a wise man.

sanskrit: ekaḥ saṃpannam aśnāti vas te vāsaś ca śobhanam yo 'saṃvibhajya bhṛtyebhyaḥ ko nṛśaṃsataras tataḥ
english: He who eats the finest food alone, who has a fine dwelling all to himself, and does not share with his dependants — who is more cruel than he?

sanskrit: ekaḥ pāpāni kurute phalaṃ bhuṅkte mahājanaḥ bhoktāro vipramucyante kartā doṣeṇa lipyate
english: One alone commits the sins, yet a great multitude enjoys the fruit; the enjoyers are freed, but the doer is tainted by the fault.

sanskrit: ekaṃ hanyān na vā hanyād iṣur mukto dhanuṣmatā buddhir buddhimatotsṛṣṭā hanyād rāṣṭraṃ sarājakam
english: An arrow shot by an archer may or may not slay one man; but intelligence unleashed by an intelligent man can destroy a whole kingdom together with its king.

sanskrit: ekayā dve viniścitya trīṃś caturbhir vaśe kuru pañca jitvā viditvā ṣaṭ sapta hitvā sukhī bhava
english: Having resolved the one, determine the two; bring the three under control with the four; having conquered the five and understood the six, abandon the seven and be happy.

sanskrit: ekaṃ viṣaraso hanti śastreṇaikaś ca vadhyate sarāṣṭraṃ saprajaṃ hanti rājānaṃ mantravisravaḥ
english: Poison kills one person; a weapon kills one person; but a breach of counsel kills a king together with his whole kingdom and people.

sanskrit: ekaḥ svādu na bhuñjīta ekaś cārthān na cintayet eko na gacched adhvānaṃ naikaḥ supteṣu jāgṛyāt
english: One should not enjoy sweet things alone, nor deliberate on important matters alone, nor travel a road alone, nor stay awake alone among those who sleep.

sanskrit: ekam evādvitīyaṃ tad yad rājan nāvabudhyase satyaṃ svargasya sopānaṃ pārāvārasya naur iva
english: O king, that which you fail to understand — the one without a second — is truth, which is the stairway to heaven, like a boat across the ocean.

sanskrit: ekaḥ kṣamāvatāṃ doṣo dvitīyo nopalabhyate yad enaṃ kṣamayā yuktam aśaktaṃ manyate janaḥ
english: There is one fault in those who are patient, and a second is not found in them: people take one who is endowed with patience to be powerless.

sanskrit: eko dharmaḥ paraṃ śreyaḥ kṣamaikā śāntir uttamā vidyaikā paramā dṛṣṭir ahiṃsaikā sukhāvahā
english: Dharma alone is the supreme good; patience alone is the highest peace; knowledge alone is the supreme vision; non-violence alone brings happiness.

sanskrit: dvāv imau grasate bhūmiḥ sarpo bilaśayān iva rājānaṃ cāviroddhāraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ cāpravāsinam
english: The earth swallows these two as a serpent swallows creatures that dwell in holes: a king who does not resist his foes, and a brahmin who does not go abroad to study.

sanskrit: dve karmaṇī naraḥ kurvann asmiṃl loke virocate abruvan paruṣaṃ kiṃ cid asato nārthayaṃs tathā
english: A man who performs two actions shines in this world: speaking no harsh word, and not seeking favour from the wicked.

sanskrit: dvāv imau puruṣavyāghra parapratyayakāriṇau striyaḥ kāmitakāminyo lokaḥ pūjitapūjakaḥ
english: O tiger among men, these two act according to another's disposition: women toward those who love them, and the world toward those who honour it.

sanskrit: dvāv imau kaṇṭakau tīkṣṇau śarīrapariśoṣaṇau yaś cādhanaḥ kāmayate yaś ca kupyaty anīśvaraḥ
english: These two are sharp thorns that wither the body: one who is poor yet consumed by desires, and one who is powerless yet given to anger.

sanskrit: dvāv imau puruṣau rājan svargasyopari tiṣṭhataḥ prabhuś ca kṣamayā yukto daridraś ca pradānavān
english: O king, these two men stand above heaven itself: the mighty one endowed with patience, and the poor man who is generous in giving.

sanskrit: nyāyāgatasya dravyasya boddhavyau dvāv atikramau apātre pratipattiś ca pātre cāpratipādanam
english: With regard to wealth lawfully acquired, two transgressions should be understood: giving it to an unworthy recipient, and withholding it from a worthy one.

sanskrit: trayo nyāyā manuṣyāṇāṃ śrūyante bharatarṣabha kanīyān madhyamaḥ śreṣṭha iti vedavido viduḥ
english: O bull of the Bhāratas, three standards are spoken of for men; those who know the Vedas understand them as the inferior, the middling, and the best.

sanskrit: trividhāḥ puruṣā rājann uttamādhamamadhyamāḥ niyojayed yathāvat tāṃs trividheṣv eva karmasu
english: O king, men are of three kinds — superior, inferior, and middling; one should employ them properly in tasks of three corresponding kinds.

sanskrit: traya evādhanā rājan bhāryā dāsas tathā sutaḥ yat te samadhigacchanti yasya te tasya tad dhanam
english: O king, only three are without independent wealth: a wife, a slave, and a son; whatever they acquire belongs to the one to whom they belong.

sanskrit: catvāri rājñā tu mahābalena; varjyāny āhuḥ paṇḍitas tāni vidyāt alpaprajñaiḥ saha mantraṃ na kuryān; na dīrghasūtrair alasaiś cāraṇaiś ca
english: Four things a king of great power should know and avoid, say the wise: he should not deliberate in counsel with those of little understanding, nor with those who are dilatory, nor with the slothful, nor with wandering minstrels.

sanskrit: catvāri te tāta gṛhe vasantu; śriyābhijuṣṭasya gṛhasthadharme vṛddho jñātir avasannaḥ kulīnaḥ; sakhā daridro bhaginī cānapatyā
english: Dear Dhṛtarāṣṭra, let these four dwell in your house, in accordance with the householder's duty for one blessed with prosperity: an aged kinsman fallen on hard times, a friend of noble birth who is poor, and a childless sister.

sanskrit: catvāry āha mahārāja sadyaskāni bṛhaspatiḥ pṛcchate tridaśendrāya tānīmāni nibodha me
english: O great king, Bṛhaspati told Indra, lord of the thirty gods, four things that bear immediate fruit — hear these from me now.

sanskrit: devatānāṃ ca saṃkalpam anubhāvaṃ ca dhīmatām vinayaṃ kṛtavidyānāṃ vināśaṃ pāpakarmaṇām
english: They are: the resolve of the gods, the majesty of the wise, the humility of those accomplished in knowledge, and the destruction of those who commit wicked deeds.

sanskrit: pañcāgnayo manuṣyeṇa paricaryāḥ prayatnataḥ pitā mātāgnir ātmā ca guruś ca bharatarṣabha
english: O bull of the Bhāratas, five fires must be tended by a man with great care: father, mother, fire, the self, and the teacher.

sanskrit: pañcaiva pūjayaṃl loke yaśaḥ prāpnoti kevalam devān pitṝn manuṣyāṃś ca bhikṣūn atithipañcamān
english: He who honours these five alone attains glory in the world: the gods, the ancestors, men, mendicants, and guests as the fifth.

sanskrit: pañca tvānugamiṣyanti yatra yatra gamiṣyasi mitrāṇy amitrā madhyasthā upajīvyopajīvinaḥ
english: Five will follow you wherever you go: friends, enemies, those who are neutral, those on whom one depends, and those who depend on one.

sanskrit: pañcendriyasya martyasya chidraṃ ced ekam indriyam tato 'sya sravati prajñā dṛteḥ pādād ivodakam
english: If even one of the five senses of a mortal man has a breach, his wisdom drains away through it as water from a hole at the foot of a water-bag.

sanskrit: ṣaḍ doṣāḥ puruṣeṇeha hātavyā bhūtim icchatā nidrā tandrī bhayaṃ krodha ālasyaṃ dīrghasūtratā
english: Six faults must be abandoned by a man who desires prosperity in this world: sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness, and procrastination.

sanskrit: ṣaḍ imān puruṣo jahyād bhinnāṃ nāvam ivārṇave apravaktāram ācāryam anadhīyānam ṛtvijam
english: A man should abandon these six as one abandons a broken boat on the ocean: a teacher who does not impart instruction, and a priest who does not study —

sanskrit: arakṣitāraṃ rājānaṃ bhāryāṃ cāpriyavādinīm grāmakāmaṃ ca gopālaṃ vanakāmaṃ ca nāpitam
english: — a king who does not protect his people, a wife who speaks unkindly, a cowherd who desires the village, and a barber who desires the forest.

sanskrit: ṣaḍ eva tu guṇāḥ puṃsā na hātavyāḥ kadā cana satyaṃ dānam anālasyam anasūyā kṣamā dhṛtiḥ
english: Yet these six qualities a man should never abandon at any time: truth, generosity, diligence, freedom from envy, patience, and steadfast courage.

sanskrit: ṣaṇṇām ātmani nityānām aiśvaryaṃ yo 'dhigacchati na sa pāpaiḥ kuto 'narthair yujyate vijitendriyaḥ
english: He who masters within himself these six that are ever-present — he who has conquered his senses — is not afflicted by sins, much less by misfortunes.

sanskrit: ṣaḍ ime ṣaṭsu jīvanti saptamo nopalabhyate corāḥ pramatte jīvanti vyādhiteṣu cikitsakāḥ
english: These six live off six others; a seventh is not found: thieves live off the careless, physicians live off the sick —

sanskrit: pramadāḥ kāmayāneṣu yajamāneṣu yājakāḥ rājā vivadamāneṣu nityaṃ mūrkheṣu paṇḍitāḥ
english: — women of loose conduct live off those consumed by desire, officiating priests live off those who perform sacrifices, a king lives off those who are quarrelsome, and the wise always live off fools.

sanskrit: sapta doṣāḥ sadā rājñā hātavyā vyasanodayāḥ prāyaśo yair vinaśyanti kṛtamūlāś ca pārthivāḥ
english: Seven faults, which give rise to vices, should always be abandoned by a king; it is by these that kings, even well-established ones, mostly meet their ruin.

sanskrit: striyo 'kṣā mṛgayā pānaṃ vākpāruṣyaṃ ca pañcamam mahac ca daṇḍapāruṣyam arthadūṣaṇam eva ca
english: Women, dice, hunting, drinking, harsh speech as the fifth, great severity of punishment, and corruption of wealth — these are the seven.
